newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance minister vows fiscal discipline.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance minister vows fiscal discipline.

text.p: Thai finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Tuesday the government would follow strict fiscal discipline and work to balance the budget as part of its efforts to improve the country's ailing economy.
Thanong said in a televised address that the government also planned to streamline the tax system and speed up the privatisation of state enterprises to take some of the burden off the government.

"These economic revival measures may depress the economy in the short term, but it would be an essential economic contraction in order to strengthen our economic foundation before we embark on further durable growth," he said.
"It is one step backward in preparation for a future of steady advances," Thanong said.
Earlier Thanong and central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi announced a series of tough measures, recommended by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), aimed at reviving the economy.

They included suspending the operation of more than half the nation's 91 finance companies, a three percentage point increase in value added tax (VAT), and strict monetary and fiscal targets for the next few years.
If the measures are properly implemented, the government hopes to receive $12-$15 billion in loans from the IMF and foreign nations, Thanong said.
Thanong said Thai people had to be willing to accept tough measures in order to lift the economy out of its biggest slump in over a decade.
"Although we must admit that the task of tackling economic problems is not easy, it is by no mean impossible," he said.
"On the contrary, I still fully believe in the fundamentals and capability of the Thai economy."
